findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The baffles of the ice machine were observed with black mold on the food contact surface. Shown to the PIC. See that the interior surfaces of the ice machine are cleaned as frequent as possible to prevent mold build up. Will followup on 6/22/2026 to ensure that baffles have been cleaned and are free of mold.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: A mini cooler along the service line was observed with an ambient temperature of 60F (probed). The PIC indicated that the cooling switch was accidentally turned off, not allowing for efficient cold holding temperatures. The food products were recently added to the cooler and items were placed on an ice bath to correct the violation. The cooler’s temperature was observed to decrease in temperature after the switch was flipped on. Ensure that cold holding equipment is sufficient enough to maintain temperatures of 41F or below.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: A second mini cooler was observed not holding proper cold holding temperatures. A portion of milk was probed at 50F. The temperature knob was placed on level 4 and the knob was turned to level 7 to make sure that the cooler is functioning properly. The cooler holds dairy products and the items were recently placed inside of the cooler. The temperature of the cooler started to decrease after adjusting the knob. Violation corrected. Ensure that the cold holding equipment is sufficient for maintaining temperatures of 41F or below.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Despite the facility being in full operation, there weren’t any sanitizer buckets present for sanitizing food contact surfaces. Discussed with PIC and a bucket was created and tested at 400ppm (quat) to correct the violation. Ensure that there is alway a sani solution available during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: The interior of the hood system was observed accumulated with dust. Shown to the PIC. A professional hood cleaning company will need to service the system to clean the duct work. Ensure that hood system is cleaned as often as necessary to prevent debris accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
At least four of the individuals working at the time of the inspection had expired food handler certificates. Be sure to get employees re-certified and compliant with food safety guidelines. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The sanitizer bucket stored along the coffee line tested at 0ppm. The PIC remade the bucket with a fresh solution and it tested at 200ppm (q). Ensure that sanitizer buckets are maintained at the manufacturer’s recommended concentration and changed at least every 4 hours in order for the chemical to properly sanitize food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment: The ice scoop’s handle was observed directly touching ice in the machine stored in the back of the house. Discussed with PIC and the ice scoop was placed inside of a bucket designated for ice scoops when not in use. Ensure that ice scoops are stored in manner that protects against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.
